objective: come up with a complete design for the episode structure for bulding episodes. Use conversation history to put together a permanent goal object for you to iterate towards and then review. show me the final plan.
authority: User-requested design work; not workflow approval or permission to implement, execute tests, commit, or publish.

scope.deliverable: Complete high-level Episode structure and lifecycle design, reviewed against the conversation and repository boundaries.
scope.product_goal: An actively used IterativeEpisodeRefiner, also an Episode-library reference, that finishes and verifies every materialization-spec'd nested Episode build through goal-directed reasoning and coding.
scope.not_a_completion_claim: This goal does not claim that the proposed refiner has been implemented or empirically validated.
scope.priority: Outcome ownership, real decision points, nested design/implementation/evaluation loops and information boundaries first; exact schemas, numerical calibration, examples and coding later.

requirements.requirement: Persist the full objective, its constraints, acceptance requirements, iteration history and review evidence.
Define the whole path from initial Builder output and boundary findings to an active refiner and a verified build or an honest unresolved result.
Accept all materialization-spec'd builds, including broken and novel nested designs; do not restrict refinement to a domain-specific example catalog.
Define root and scoped outcome ownership, with refinement nesting independent of the Target Workflow architecture.
Make design itself a nested Episode workflow with independently judged parts and a parent responsible for the combined design.
Identify RefineImplementation as the actual coding Episode, with its own iterative local measurement and credit.
Keep VerifyBehavior as independent parent acceptance, not the coding Episode's internal measurement mechanism.
Explain how target-specific behavior, evidence, decomposition and measurement grounding produce faithful assignments, including the limits of automatic semantic judgment.
Define every Episode role's goal, inputs, repeated unit, allowed children, outputs, authority and basis of local progress.
Preserve host-owned admission, evidence-based yield, credit, rarefaction and registered continuation at every Episode level.
Separate goal satisfaction, numerical return, incomplete yield exhaustion, blocking and external termination; already-correct work returns without invented repairs.
Provide one editable shared specification/code workspace, compact review state, immutable evaluation snapshots and evidence invalidation.
Let authorized refinement Episodes request real host-mediated validation Runs using existing executors, with distinct lineage and preserved isolation.
Preserve zero yield for failure alone, admitted durable learning, replay safety, duplicate-credit prevention and ordinary credit admission for repaired representations.
State the proposed designer authority extension explicitly; freeze active contracts, retain human authority over semantic changes, and do not widen ordinary task Episode authority.
Specify feedback destinations, recursion, scope escalation, dependency cycles and the difference between child return and ending refinement.
Review the structure against success, failure, bad design, nested prerequisites, conflicting changes, missing evidence and interrupted execution.
Map the design to inspected repository components and distinguish existing foundations from required extensions.
Complete a requirement-by-requirement review, resolve structural contradictions, and present the final proposed plan to the user.
Keep example collection, detailed score formulas and implementation later; run no further product tests and make no production changes for this design goal.
Nest the implementer inside the actual Designer, whose goal includes realizing and evaluating its design rather than returning a paper work order.
Place parts-making and selection above the Designer, judging each selected part by its contribution to the enclosing whole.

Review every nesting as a genuine choice, a required prerequisite, or a required evaluation on return; do not turn a serial dependency into an arbitrary menu of sibling activities. Support nested resolution of design decisions where that is a real subproblem.

Design each Episode as an information boundary: distinguish durable audit, child-local iteration state, and bounded parent-specific reports; preserve evidence lineage and applicable attempt history against circular reasoning, repeat errors and stale conclusions; share only relevant dependency projections between siblings, without relying on free-form LLM summaries.
Use a reusable Designer specialized through prepared instructions and examples, with optional library support search and a general route for unfamiliar tasks.
Treat numerical-controller design, including credit, rarefaction and continuation, as one coupled design assignment.
Only Parts owners create Designer assignments or nested Parts scopes. Specialists cannot create designers directly or indirectly; new design subproblems return to the owner with their evidence.

Expose candidate/check changes and regressions during child iteration, detect possible repair cycles across levels, preserve shared history, and route coupled failures to a joint assignment without repeated credit for restoring an old state.

Confirm the evidence-based implementation boundary: concentrated refiner/library code with explicitly identified shared integration changes, staged activation, compatibility verification and a reviewable merge plan; do not guarantee zero breakage.

Finalize the editable design and provide concrete copyable implementation goal statements with completion evidence, while keeping implementation and test execution unauthorized until separately requested.

completion_rule: The authoritative plan covers every requirement without contradictory ownership or undefined feedback paths; the review records evidence for every requirement and no unresolved structural findings; the final plan is presented. User approval and implementation remain distinct later actions.

iteration_history.evidence: At goal resumption the saved v0 plan still used RefineObligation and placed VerifyBehavior inside its local coding loop; recent conversational refinements had not been reconciled into the permanent design.
iteration_history.next_action: Replace the stale draft with the complete ownership and nested-design architecture, then audit it.

iteration_history.evidence: The v1 draft established Parts -> Designer -> Implementer ownership and distinguished local measurement from parent acceptance. Subsequent conversation exposed two incomplete areas: permitted-child lists did not specify prerequisite/return control, and typed handoffs did not yet specify local memory versus parent steering information.
iteration_history.next_action: Reconcile the actual control flow and information contracts before completing the structural review; v1 is not the final plan.

iteration_history.evidence: Design v2 defines decision-driven nesting, residual-design recursion, explicit prerequisite/return continuations, coding and measurement authority, and local-state versus parent-report contracts. The review maps all 24 requirements, walks successful and adverse paths, and checks report sufficiency against parent decisions. No unresolved structural contradiction was found in this self-review; no production tests or implementation were performed.
iteration_history.next_action: Present the high-level proposal for discussion. Approval, exact executable contracts, numerical calibration, implementation and empirical validation remain separate later work.

iteration_history.evidence: The user refined the design after v2: specialization can be supplied as instructions/examples, numerical control stays together, and repair cycles make autonomous designer recursion unsafe. Final design v3 removes that recursion, assigns all new design work to Parts owners, requires in-loop shared regression reporting, identifies the code/integration boundary, and adds seven copyable implementation goals. The v3 review supersedes v2 where those decisions differ. Only documentation changed; no product tests ran.
iteration_history.next_action: Hand off the finalized design and implementation goals. Begin Goal 1 only when the user assigns it; do not infer implementation, testing or publication authority from this design finalization.

completion_scope: Finalized high-level design, code/integration boundary, seven future implementation goals and a requirement-by-requirement self-review. Not executable workflow approval, implementation completion, or evidence of runtime success.
